extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers and newspaper editors/wire-service staff
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and packaging short wire-service news dispatches for a newspaper/front‑page/news‑bulletin (dateline, attribution, short items) during wartime; focuses on labeling, attribution, and freedom-of-press norms evident in the copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: News of official matters should be made freely available
rubrics_metrics.description: "News of official matters should be made freely available in all Other nations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement appears as a normative principle urged by a press congress in context: the press urged that governmental favoritism be discontinued and that official matters be made freely available internationally. (Verbatim sentence from page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinue governmental favoritism to newspapers/press associations
rubrics_metrics.description: "Press, urging that governmental favoritism to individual newspapers or press associations be discontinued..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expressed as a recommendation from a press congress—i.e., governments should not favor particular newspapers or press associations; included as part of the rationale for forming an inter‑American press society and for protecting free reporting. (Verbatim phrase from page.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Label delayed dispatches/datelines clearly
rubrics_metrics.description: Use explicit delayed labels and datelines (e.g., "AUSTRALAA, June 8—(Delayed)—").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page shows practice of marking delayed reports in the dateline. Example on page: "AUSTRALAA, June 8—(Delayed)— (AP) Another decoration..." Use of '(Delayed)' in the dateline signals latency of the dispatch and should be applied where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include dateline and wire-service credit
rubrics_metrics.description: Include city and date datelines and wire-service credit (e.g., "Havana, June 12 (A. P.).—").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple items on the page use city+date datelines and an Associated Press credit in parentheses; this demonstrates the standard practice of providing provenance and time for short news items. Example verbatim: "Havana, June 12 (A. P.).—The Cuban Navy..."

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute recorded broadcasts and special-source material
rubrics_metrics.description: When using recorded broadcasts or non‑original material, label and attribute the source (e.g., "[broadcast was recorded by the Associated Press.]").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page contains bracketed notes indicating that a broadcast was recorded by the AP; this models the editorial criterion of explicitly attributing recorded or re‑aired material so readers know the source and nature of the item.
